nodes.name: Sooner or later an agent needs a credential: an API key to…
nodes.text: Sooner or later an agent needs a credential: an API key to call a service, a deployment token, a signing file. The easy answer is to paste it into the prompt or commit it to a file the agent can read. Both work once. Both leave a copy somewhere nobody tracks, readable by anything that can read that place.

nodes.name: The underlying problem is that a password says nothing…
nodes.text: The underlying problem is that a password says nothing about who should use it or for what. Teams need the opposite: a credential stored once, with an explicit list of who may read it, and a record of when it was revealed.

nodes.name: NullDull keeps credentials in Secrets, a library separate…
nodes.text: NullDull keeps credentials in Secrets, a library separate from ordinary Memory files. It holds environment sets, login credentials and private files. Ordinary Memory access never grants secret access, and sharing a file or a location does not share its secrets.

nodes.name: Each secret has its own grants—for seeing that it exists,…
nodes.text: Each secret has its own grants—for seeing that it exists, reading or exporting its value, writing a new version and managing access. Workspace owners and admins can set defaults so new secrets start with sensible access, while individual grants and removals stay explicit. Secrets live in the same folder tree as a location’s files, so a team can group them by provider or purpose.

nodes.name: Values are encrypted at rest with a fresh key for every…
nodes.text: Values are encrypted at rest with a fresh key for every version, wrapped by a managed key service. This is server-side encryption at rest, not end-to-end encryption: it protects stored data, not an authorized reader or a copy someone has already exported.

nodes.name: An agent connection does not inherit a member’s secret…
nodes.text: An agent connection does not inherit a member’s secret access automatically. Secrets is its own capability—none, read, write or read-write—and it is off by default. What an agent can do with a secret is the overlap of that delegation and the member’s current grant on that secret.

nodes.name: When an agent does need a value, the client can import a…
nodes.text: When an agent does need a value, the client can import a secret from a local file or export one to a new local file without the value passing through the conversation. Export creates the file with owner-only permissions and never overwrites an existing file. Revealing a value into the agent’s context is possible too, and treated for what it is: the value is then visible to the model and its harness. The in-app agent, Null, has no Secrets tools at all.

nodes.name: Some actions stay in the browser.
nodes.text: ## Some actions stay in the browser.

nodes.name: Granting access, changing defaults and approving a…
nodes.text: Granting access, changing defaults and approving a requested review are browser actions. A requested review of a new secret value needs a different member with current read and write access to approve it. An agent can propose; it cannot approve, and it cannot widen its own access.

nodes.name: In the browser, revealed values clear after 60 seconds,…
nodes.text: In the browser, revealed values clear after 60 seconds, when you hide them, or when you navigate away. They are not written to browser storage or URLs.

nodes.name: Connections expire six calendar months after approval and…
nodes.text: Connections expire six calendar months after approval and can be revoked from Settings at any time. Removing a member removes their grants. Every request rechecks the current state, so a revoked connection stops working on its next call.

nodes.name: Revocation cannot recall a value that was already exported…
nodes.text: Revocation cannot recall a value that was already exported or revealed; no system can. What it can do is make sure the next use requires a permission that still exists. That is the trade we want: agents that can do real work with credentials, under permissions a person can read, change and take back.
